newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Tesa sees weak 1997 turnover.
newsitem.headline: German Tesa sees weak 1997 turnover.

text.p: Tesa, the adhesive tape unit of German cosmetics and medication maker Beiersdorf, warned on Monday that it expected flat, or even slightly falling, revenues for 1997.
Overcapacity, that had led to a fierce price war to maintain market share, was the reason for the poor outlook, Beiersdorf board member Dieter Steinmeyer told a news briefing in Frankfurt.
He said that for 1996 Tesa produced a small loss on revenues of 1.31 billion marks compared to sales of 1.28 billion in 1995. A break-even was only possible in 1998, he added.
